function_question: How does nature make things easy to see in the dark?

opening.text: There was a girl called Nika who loved staying at Grandpa Sam's house, with its big wild garden full of vegetables and birds.
After dinner, Grandpa walked down the dark garden path to check on his tomatoes, and Nika watched from the window.
Grandpa tripped on the path and nearly fell. "I won't put up a big lamp," he said. "It would wake the birds in the hedge."

card.problem: Grandpa trips on the dark path at night
card.goal: Mark the path so it can be seen at night
card.rules: No electricity and no bright lamps

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: A trip in the dark
chapters.line: Nika wonders: how can Grandpa see his path without waking the birds?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Nika needs a night partner
chapters.line: A dark garden needs two sharp-eyed designers. Will you join Nika?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Nika meet heroes that glow and shine in the dark.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of reflect and glow
chapters.line: The heroes share how to shine without making much light.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The torch hunt
chapters.line: Nika switches off the lights and hands you a small torch.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: Grandpa's empathy map
chapters.line: To help Grandpa, first you have to really understand him.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great path starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The night test
chapters.line: Some markers vanish in the dark. You fix them, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: A safe walk home
chapters.line: Grandpa walks the whole path, and the birds keep sleeping.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Grandpa Sam keeps tripping on his garden path at night, but a bright lamp would wake the birds. Can you help Nika light his way? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a spark of an idea for seeing in the dark. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been shining in the dark for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes of the night!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which card will shine back brightest in your torch beam? Clear the floor before you turn off the lights.
guide.sketch: Time to draw Grandpa's path from above, like a real designer!
guide.build_and_test: Build 5 markers and line them up in a dark room. How many can you see from 3 metres away?
guide.retry_tip: Designers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing, like the angle or the material, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Grandpa Sam walks his garden path every night with YOUR markers showing the way, and the birds sleep soundly in the hedge.

quick_check.question: Grandpa's path is 6 metres long. Nika puts a marker every 1 metre, starting 1 metre from the back door. How many markers does she need?
quick_check.right: Right! Markers at 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 metres make 6 markers.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Try counting: 1 metre, 2 metres, 3 metres… all the way to 6.

clue_cards.name: Firefly
clue_cards.trick: It makes light inside its body.
clue_cards.does: Almost no energy is lost as heat, so its glow is cool to touch.

clue_cards.name: Glow-worm
clue_cards.trick: It shines a blue-green light on a cave ceiling.
clue_cards.does: Insects fly to the glow and get stuck on its sticky silk threads.

clue_cards.name: Cat
clue_cards.trick: A mirror layer at the back of each eye.
clue_cards.does: It bounces light back, so its eyes shine in a torch beam.

clue_cards.name: Herring
clue_cards.trick: Scales full of tiny flat crystals, like mirrors.
clue_cards.does: They flash brightly when even a little light hits them.

predict.prompt: Makes its own light, or bounces light back? Predict first!
predict.explain: Fireflies make their own light. A bike reflector and the Moon make none at all: they bounce back light from a torch or from the Sun.

lab.title: The torch hunt lab
lab.predict: In a dark room, with a torch next to your eyes, which card will shine back brightest from 3 metres?
lab.measure: brightness score (0 = can't see it, 5 = dazzling)

tool.name: Empathy Map
tool.intro: An Empathy Map helps you understand the person you are designing for. It has 4 boxes: Says, Thinks, Does and Feels. Today you'll learn the first 2: Says and Does.

parts.name: Says
parts.what: Write down the exact words the person says.
parts.example: 🚲 A rider says: "My chain keeps slipping off!"
parts.starter: When Nika asks about the path, Grandpa says: "…"

parts.name: Does
parts.what: Watch what the person actually does.
parts.example: 🚲 The rider checks the chain every morning before riding.
parts.starter: At night on the path, Grandpa…

sketch_checklist: I drew the path from above with all my markers.
I labelled which markers reflect and which ones glow.
I wrote how far apart and how high my markers are.

test.measure: markers seen from 3 m in a dark room (out of 5)
test.check_question: Bird check: do your markers stay gentle enough not to wake the birds?
check_options: Yes, they only reflect or glow softly

reflection.question: Which nature trick lit Grandpa's way home?
